data.title: ARC Awarded $10.9M Contract with Army DEVCOM Armaments Center to Advance Small Unit Resupply in Contested Environments
data.description:
ARC Awarded $10.9M Contract with Army DEVCOM Armaments Center to Advance Small Unit Resupply in Contested Environments

Armaments Research Company (ARC), Inc., a leader in advanced defense technology solutions, has been awarded a three-year, $10.9 million contract with the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC) through the Defense Ordnance Technology Consortium (DOTC) to continue its work transforming small unit resupply (SUR). Building on ARC’s prior SBIR Phase III task order with DEVCOM, this award advances the Army’s effort to solve the longstanding challenge of efficiently sustaining combat units at the front line in contested environments using autonomous platforms.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261029873012/en/

Over the three-year effort, ARC will further develop, integrate, and demonstrate its AI-enabled weapon sensors (AEWS) to operationalize SUR capabilities.

Over the three-year effort, ARC will further develop, integrate, and demonstrate its AI-enabled weapon sensors (AEWS) to operationalize SUR capabilities. The broader SUR architecture includes inventory management, and autonomous resupply platforms; connecting weapon data from the tactical edge with enterprise-level logistics and command-and-control integration systems. By capturing real-time weapon and ammunition data at the source, ARC’s sensors are being developed to enable predictive logistics, give commanders greater situational awareness of unit status, and support automated ammunition resupply so that distributed formations are resupplied at the time of need. ARC’s modular open system approach (MOSA) and technology platform is designed to adapt seamlessly as requirements and autonomous resupply platforms evolve.

“We’re proud to deepen our partnership with DEVCOM Armaments Center and continue building next-generation autonomous small unit resupply,” said Mike Canty, CEO of ARC. “Autonomy is changing how forces are sustained on the modern battlefield. This award pairs AEWS sensing with autonomy to increase warfighter survivability and lethality. We’re excited about the impact this capability can have across the force.”

This award reflects the Army’s continued commitment to rapid innovation and to collaborating with industry through flexible acquisition pathways like DOTC, accelerating the delivery of critical sustainment capabilities to America’s warfighters.

ABOUT ARMAMENTS RESEARCH COMPANY:

Armaments Research Company (ARC) is a technology company developing artificial intelligence-enabled weapons sensors for Enhanced Situational Awareness and Predictive Logistics in support of Large-Scale Combat Operations. Discover more at www.armaments.us.

data.title: Microsoft is winning the cloud wars and becoming Wall Street's new golden child
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone and Emily Bary

Various factors indicate that Microsoft is in a better financial position than its cloud rivals, analysts say

CEO Satya Nadella has won back Wall Street's trust.

After spending a good chunk of the past year in Wall Street's doghouse, Microsoft currently stands as the winner among the major cloud companies.

Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza issued that verdict following Amazon.com's (AMZN) Thursday earnings report, which showed cloud growth coming up short of what some investors were expecting.

Amazon's cloud business increased revenue at a 39% clip in the third quarter, while analysts tracked by FactSet had been expecting 37% growth. But institutional investors had been targeting growth more in the neighborhood of 43% to 44%, various analysts noted ahead of Amazon's report.

See also: Amazon's stock drops - even in the face of a bold new cloud forecast

The report from Amazon makes Microsoft (MSFT) "look even better," Favuzza wrote in a note to clients. That's even with the "frustrating price action" seen in Thursday's regular session, as Microsoft's stock gave back its early gains to close fractionally lower.

Microsoft's cloud growth seemed to sit better with Wall Street. The company increased revenue in its Azure cloud business by 48% in the September quarter, above a forecast for 44% to 45% growth that the company had offered back in September. And the company projected growth of 49% to 50% for the December quarter.

Favuzza wrote that the "tactical pecking order" among the big cloud companies seems to have Microsoft on top, followed by Meta Platforms (META), Amazon and then Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), which just saw its worst one-day stock decline on record.

Microsoft also stands out from the bunch because of its free cash flow, according to Greg Halter, the director of research at Carnegie Investment Counsel. The other three companies reported negative free cash flow for the third quarter, meaning that they spent more on infrastructure, data centers and related purchases than they generated in cash through their businesses. Microsoft's free cash flow stayed positive.

"We pay a lot of attention to FCF, and the market may be trying to instill some spending discipline into these companies," Halter said.

He hearkened back to the idea of "bond vigilantes," a famous term coined by economist Ed Yardeni to describe investors who shun debt until yields rise and they get paid more. Now, he noted, we might be looking at a case of "AI-spending vigilantes." Investors are drawing a hard line against companies deemed to be spending excessively without the returns to show for it.

Don't miss: Microsoft to raise up to $25 billion in bond market as investors get pickier about AI debt binge

Another thing working in Microsoft's favor is that the company "did more with less" - meaning that it was able to beat expectations with its Azure cloud growth even while capital expenditures, or infrastructure-related spending, came in $5 billion lower than the company had been modeling.

That's according to Patrick Walravens, the head of technology equity research at Citizens, who told MarketWatch that Microsoft's AI strategy is broadly resonating with customers.

"As AI advances faster and faster, the key thing enterprises are looking for is trust," he said. "Microsoft under [CEO Satya] Nadella's leadership has made trust a core part of its AI strategy, giving enterprises the ability to run, govern and distribute AI while retaining control of their data, models and intellectual property."

-Hannah Pedone -Emily Bary

data.title: 'He was heartbroken': My husband's kids abandoned him when he was dying. Was he right to leave everything to me?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'In the end, he left them a few sentimental mementos, some collectibles and old photographs'

"I'm still angry with them for the way they treated their father, especially when he was dying and needed them most." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

My situation was the opposite of the one in this letter (My partner of 17 years left me his $1 million home. His children are livid. Am I obliged to split it with them?). When I met my husband, he had essentially been on his own for nearly 20 years. He was a wonderful father who helped his children in every way he could, and he was just as devoted to my kids - a true go-to guy. He was truly the love of my life.

For the last six years of his life, he was terminally ill, and I was his full-time caregiver, around the clock. My kids, who had homes and children of their own, would drop everything to help us whenever they could. His kids, on the other hand, were both single, childless adults in their 50s, yet they never lifted a finger. No matter how much he begged them to help us, they rarely called and didn't even visit him during the last three years of his life.

He was heartbroken by their careless indifference. In the end, he left them a few mementos, some collectibles and old photographs. I inherited everything else. I still gave both of his children some money, and I've set aside a portion of my portfolio for them as well, should it outlive me, because that's simply who I am. But I'm still angry with them for the way they treated their father, especially when he was dying and needed them most.

No father deserves that kind of indifference from his own children.

Wife, Mother and Now Widow

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My abusive ex-husband promised $20,000 for our kids' education. Now he refuses to pay. Is he legally obligated?

We should, for better or for worse, be wary of making judgments about how much someone's children did or did not care.

Dear Wife,

Sometimes the hardest thing to do in life is to accept people for who they are. And when it comes to inheritance, there's often no right or wrong answer.

The tension many people experience in relationships is the expectation that they will be somebody they're not or do something they will never do. This can last for years, even decades, and despite hopeful moments of decency and respite from perceived indifference, unreliable people will show you who they are time and again, if you let them. That is a tragedy when it comes to parents and children who will never meet each other's needs. It can also bring a measure of clarity.

Your late husband seems to have reached that painful realization during his chronic illness. He saw who showed up for him, and he could see with clear-eyed perspective, perhaps for the first time, who did not support him through that difficult time. For you, it must have been painful to witness, especially because you knew just how much your husband needed and wanted their love and support. An absence of kindness at such a vulnerable time is heartbreaking.

But that clarity can also be freeing. He could finally see, perhaps, the faithful people in his life, the people who showed up and, importantly, showed that they cared. It's possible to show up and tick a box but not actually do any emotional heavy lifting, like spending time with an ailing friend or relative one-on-one or even picking up the phone to say, "I was thinking about you. I'm just checking in." That can mean as much as offering a lift to the doctor's office or the salon.

Life after a chronic illness

We should, for better or for worse, also be wary about making judgments about how much his children did or did not care. Your husband acknowledged that relationship by leaving his children items with important sentimental value. Estrangement, fear of illness, an unresolved family saga, emotional anxiety and, yes, blunt avoidance can lead to hurtful behavior. Understanding why someone acted as they did can help foster compassion for others and, importantly, for oneself.

Oasis Hospice Care, which has facilities in Houston and Austin, explores the question: Why do some friends and loved ones disappear after a chronic illness diagnosis? "Many people genuinely care but feel uncomfortable discussing illness. They may worry about saying the wrong thing, making the situation worse, or triggering difficult emotions. Instead of reaching out imperfectly, some choose silence," the organization wrote. "Unfortunately, that silence can feel like abandonment."

Leaving his children items with important sentimental value honored their relationship and their history.

"For some friends, seeing someone they care about struggle can trigger fears about aging, disability, vulnerability, or mortality," it adds. "Rather than processing those emotions, they may unconsciously withdraw. Friendships often develop around shared experiences: traveling, dining out, sports, community events, active hobbies. When chronic illness limits participation in those activities, friendships sometimes struggle to adapt."

Friends and some family members who aren't willing to adjust to the new normal may slowly fade away, the organization says. "Many people report feeling shocked by who stays and who leaves. Sometimes casual acquaintances become incredible sources of support, while long-term friends disappear. It's important to remember that another person's inability to handle illness often reflects their limitations - not your worth."

Staying true to your convictions

Your own children showed up for your husband, and that must have meant everything. Anyone who experiences chronic illness and re-evaluates the relationships in their life will tell you that there are many gifts and revelations during that time; they may be surprising or disappointing at the time, but ultimately allow you to focus on the people who care about you. Your husband had many people who were there for him, and he adjusted his estate plan accordingly.

He stayed true to his convictions and did not bow to social pressure or pressure from family members to leave his children a substantial amount in his will. That was his decision to make, and he was entitled to distribute his estate as he saw fit. He had you, of course, but leaving his children items with important sentimental value honored their relationship and their history, without giving away a large chunk of his estate to people who did not show up during his time of need.

Your late husband had you, your own children, and other friends who chose to show up for him. As much as the absence of his own children hurt, you were all there for him, and he remembered that in his will. Your husband sounds like a stand-up guy and, honestly, plenty of people in your position would move on and leave their stepchildren nothing in their will. You are making sure you dignify those relationships, in your own way.

Perhaps it's a posthumous show of respect to the man you loved, and also a refusal to allow his children's behavior to turn you into someone you don't want to be.

Related: 'Fancy cars hold no appeal': We have a 99% chance of outliving our life savings. Why not spend, spend, spend?

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

My husband wants to sell our $1.5 million home and downsize. But this is where we raised our kids - and I can't bear to leave.

-Quentin Fottrell

data.title: Pet Service Holding Announces Improved 2026 Half-Year Results and Confirms 2026 Annual Revenue Outlook of €17-18 Million
data.description:
Pet Service Holding Announces Improved 2026 Half-Year Results and Confirms 2026 Annual Revenue Outlook of €17-18 Million

The company also intends to raise up to €4 million in equity to support its growth strategy towards €50 million in revenue by 2029-2030

Regulatory News:

Pet Service Holding NV (Euronext Growth Paris, ISIN: NL0015001HZ9 / Ticker: ALPET), active in the European market for veterinary products, animal healthcare, and premium pet supplies (the “Company” or “PSH”), today presents its results for the first six months of 2026 and outlines the strategic initiatives intended to strengthen its financial position and drive further growth.

With five complementary business pillars, an improved gross margin and a proposed capital increase through a private placement of €3.5 million to €4 million, the Company aims to reach pro forma positive equity of approximately €3.7 million to €4.2 million by the end of 2026 and to continue to expand further in the European pet products market with an ambition to reach at least €50 million in revenue in 2029-2030.

Pet Service Holding generated revenue of €7.4 million in the first six months of 2026. Sales of goods increased by 7.4%. The gross margin on sales of goods improved from 33% to 35%. The operating businesses generated positive EBITDA of €30,000, compared with €16,000 a year earlier.

This performance was achieved despite the loss of a significant portion of prescription veterinary medicine sales as a result of regulations and their interpretation by the Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA). Strong growth at the other online consumer platforms, Petlux’s first revenue contribution and an improved product mix offset a significant part of this revenue loss.

After holding company expenses, Group EBITDA was negative at €226,000. The net loss was €908,000, partly reflecting holding costs, financing expenses, depreciation and amortisation, and costs associated with the Group’s continued development and integration.

Capital measures could restore positive equity of more than €4.2 million

A key priority for Pet Service Holding is to further strengthen its balance sheet and create financial flexibility to implement its growth strategy. The Company is preparing the conversion of approximately €1.025 million of convertible bonds into shares before yearend. In addition, it is working on a share issue through a private placement coordinated by NPEX1, targeting gross proceeds of €3.5 million to €4 million.

Based on negative equity of €819,000 at 30 June 2026, the successful completion of both measures would result in pro forma positive equity of approximately €3.7 million to €4.2 million, before share issuance costs, future earnings or losses, and other changes in equity.

Pet Service Holding is also working on refinancing its owned real estate assets and further improving its liquidity position.

The Company aims to restore positive equity before the end of 2026. The final timing and amount of the capital strengthening depend on the successful implementation of the financing the Group's operating performance.

Legal claims exceeding €2 million against the sellers of Asklepios

Pet Service Holding has filed legal claims against the sellers and former shareholders of Asklepios B.V., the company behind, among others, Pharmacy4Pets. The claims relate to alleged misrepresentations and/or fraud in connection with the sale of the shares in Asklepios.

The Company is claiming €1.051 million, plus statutory interest, as a reduction of the original purchase price. It is also bringing an additional claim for €1.015 million based, among other grounds, on directors’ liability.

The total claims therefore amount to approximately €2.07 million, excluding statutory interest. As a prudent estimate, Pet Service Holding has recognised only €240,000 as a receivable on its balance sheet. The remaining amounts claimed have not been recognised as income.

The Company will continue to pursue its claims through appropriate legal proceedings. A successful outcome could provide an additional positive financial contribution, but the outcome and the amount of any compensation remain uncertain.

Budget Pets: a key driver of the European growth strategy

Through Budget Pets, Pet Service Holding is developing a discount retail chain for pet food, pet supplies and accessories. Following the opening of its first store in Bussum in July 2026, preparations are under way for a second store at the De Lely shopping centre in Arnhem-Noord. The store is expected to open during the first week of December 2026.

The new store will have more than 500 m² of retail space and will be located in a shopping centre anchored by Jumbo and Lidl, two major supermarket chains that attract substantial customer traffic. The centre attracts an estimated 1.6 million visitors per year. Based on its current commercial assumptions, Pet Service Holding expects the Arnhem-Noord store could generate annual revenue of approximately €1.5 million once fully operational and with an established customer base.

In its initial expansion phase, the Company aims to establish at least 15 Budget Pets stores in the Netherlands. A subsequent phase envisages expanding the network to 50 locations, with Belgium and Germany also being evaluated as potential growth markets.

Five strategic pillars and annual revenue potential exceeding €20 million

Pet Service Holding now has five complementary business pillars: Aesculaap, the online consumer platforms (including Dierapotheek.com and Pharmacy4Pets.com), Petlux, RHR Cat-Trees and Budget Pets.

Following the acquisition of the business activities of RHR Cat-Trees in July 2026 and the addition of Budget Pets, management estimates that the Group’s combined activities represent annual revenue potential of more than €20 million. This potential could first be achieved over a full financial year in 2027, excluding any further acquisitions or expansion of the existing activities.

As part of the RHR Cat-Trees transaction, inventory with an original purchase-cost value of approximately €1 million was acquired for €325,000 by Pet Service Holding. The Company expects this inventory to generate approximately €2 million in gross sales across 2026 and 2027 combined.

The resumption of supplies by Royal Canin in October 2026, initially through Budget Pets, also creates additional commercial opportunities.

Based on these developments, the Company remains confident in reaching revenue of approximately €17–18 million in 2026.

Strategic ambition of at least €50 million in Group revenue by 2029 - 2030

Pet Service Holding set a new ambition to achieve consolidated Group revenue of at least €50 million by 2029-2030. The further roll-out of Budget Pets, international distribution of premium products, growth of the online consumer platforms and further integration of existing activities are expected to contribute jointly to this ambition. Achieving this growth ambition expressly depends on successful completion of the proposed share issue, sufficient financing and successful commercial and operational execution.

Ron van Veldhoven, CEO of Pet Service Holding, commented:

“Pet Service Holding is entering an important new phase in its development. Over the past few years, we have invested in building a European platform with five complementary business pillars. The improvement in our gross margin confirms that the continued optimisation of our activities is delivering results.

Our next step is to strengthen our financial position. With the proposed bond conversions and share issue, we could achieve pro forma positive equity of approximately €3.7 million to €4.2 million. This would provide a solid foundation for further growth.

With Budget Pets, we also have a concept that we believe is highly scalable. The second store in Arnhem is scheduled to open in early December and represents another step towards establishing a nationwide and, ultimately, international retail network.

These developments together with the trend observed in H2 2026, should enable us to reach €17-18 million in revenue by the end of 2026.

Our new ambition of at least €50 million in Group revenue by 2029 - 2030 is substantial, but it is based on the further development of our existing activities and the growth opportunities we see within our five pillars. With successful financing and disciplined execution, we aim to deliver this next phase of growth.”

Publication of the 2026 half-year report

The half-year report of Pet Service Holding N.V. for the first six months of 2026, including the management report, financial results, an explanation of the financing strategy and the risk analysis, will be made available through the Company’s usual publication channels.

About Pet Service Holding NV

Pet Service Holding NV is a leading player in the pet care sector in the Netherlands. The company distinguishes itself in this competitive market by bringing together a broad range of services and leveraging its valuable experience and expertise in the field. With a focus on pet supplies, nutrition, and products for veterinary practices, Pet Service Holding is well positioned to meet the needs of pets and their owners throughout Europe.

data.title: Fluence Energy (FLNC) Faces Securities Class Action Amid Inability to Ramp Houston Facility
data.description:
Fluence Energy (FLNC) Faces Securities Class Action Amid Inability to Ramp Houston Facility

Fluence Energy (FLNC) Faces Securities Class Action Amid Inability to Ramp Houston Facility

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 30, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fluence Energy (NASDAQ: FLNC) faces a securities class action, which seeks to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Fluence securities between November 24, 2025 and September 16, 2026. Hagens Berman urges Fluence investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now.

The suit follows a stream of unexpected earnings announcements that were apparently at odds with Fluence's assurances that it was positioned to capitalize on surging demand for data centers, and which collectively wiped out roughly $3 billion of the company's market capitalization.

National shareholders rights firm Hagens Berman continues its investigation into claims that Fluence violated the federal securities laws.

The firm urges Fluence investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now. In addition, persons with knowledge who may be able to assist the investigation are invited to contact the firm's attorneys.

Class Period: Nov. 24, 2025 – Sept. 16, 2026
Lead Plaintiff Deadline: Nov. 27, 2026
Visit: www.hbsslaw.com/FLNC
Direct Contact Email: FLNC@hbsslaw.com
Firm Telephone: 844-916-0895
Video: https://youtu.be/KVTyrrRmmqM

Fluence Energy, Inc. ($FLNC) Securities Class Action:

The litigation's focus is on the propriety of Fluence's assurances that it was "well positioned to capitalize on the accelerating demand for energy storage[,]" and its backlog sufficiently covered revenue expectations. The company's plan depended on successfully ramping its "fully automated" Houston manufacturing facility's production of thermal management systems for its Gridstack ProTM battery energy storage solutions.

The complaint alleges that Fluence did not disclose important information to investors – its ability to deliver on its backlog and recognize revenue depended on new contract facilities that included incomplete and non-operational facilities. The complaint also alleges the company did not disclose that facility remediation efforts were unsuccessful.

Investors began to learn the truth through a series of partial disclosures beginning on February 4, 2026. That day, Fluence reported its Q1 2026 results included a significant year-over-year margin compression due to "additional estimated costs on two projects[]" and a significant year-over-year increase in net losses.

Then, on August 5, 2026 Fluence announced its Q3 2026 results included weaker than expected revenues, a massive year-over-year margin compression, and a net loss of $44.3 million compared to net income of $6.2 million in the same quarter last year.

The company said it "now expects that $400 million in project deliveries will be delayed into fiscal 2027 due to production issues at a new international contract facility[]" and also blamed "construction related delays that affected the completion and start-up of a new U.S. contract manufacturing facility."

Finally, on September 16, 2026 Fluence slashed its 2026 revenue guidance again (by 20%). CEO Julian Nebreda Marquez blamed the continuing "delays in the ramp up of our contract manufacturing facility in Houston." He also revealed the ramp delay was caused by having to manually weld rather than employing the automated welding process.

Each of these revelations triggered sharp declines in the price of Fluence shares. Between the first partial disclosure on February 4 and September 17, 2026 shares have fallen $21.33 (-73%).

"We're focused on when the Houston welding issue was first known to Fluence management given the facility's crucial role in onshoring," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lincoln Educational Services Corporation (NASDAQ: LINC) faces a securities class action seeking to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Lincoln Educational securities between May 11, 2026 and August 9, 2026. The suit follows the company's August 10, 2026 announcement of Q2 2026 results containing a surprisingly slow student starts metric which drove the price of company shares down $10.22 (-24.9%).

The developments have prompted national shareholders rights firm Hagens Berman to open an investigation into claims that Lincoln Educational violated the securities laws.

The firm encourages Lincoln Educational investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now. Persons with knowledge who may be able to assist the investigation are invited to contact the firm's attorneys.

Direct Contact Email: LINC@hbsslaw.com 
Firm Telephone: 844-916-0895
Video: https://youtu.be/YGTj5V-AZGw

Lincoln Educational Services Corporation ($LINC) Securities Class Action:

The lawsuit is focused on the propriety of Lincoln Educational's statements about its student starts, a metric that features prominently within the company's financial reports.

On May 11, 2026, Lincoln Educational reported its Q1 2026 earnings and held its related investor call. Among other things, management emphasized "'[t]he 19.5% student start growth during the first quarter exceeded our expectations, which has led to increasing our student start growth guidance for the full year to between 10% and 14%."  During the related investor call, management emphasized "the continuing momentum in our business" and "strong, sustained demand" in the business.

The market reacted favorably to the news and narrative going forward, sending the price of Lincoln Educational shares up $4.75 (+10.6%) that day.

Investors' expectations were dashed on August 10, 2026, when the company reported its Q2 2026 earnings and held its related investor call. Of significant concern was the revelation that student starts grew a paltry 1%, seemingly at odds with the "continuing momentum" and "strong, sustained demand" narrative conveyed just three months earlier. In addition, management said "[d]uring the first quarter of this year, we achieved student start growth of nearly 20%, and we expected second quarter start growth to moderate to approximately half this rate."

This news drove the price of Lincoln Educational shares down $10.22 (-24.9%), wiping out over $300 million of the company's market capitalization in a single day.

"We're focused on whether Lincoln Educational may have intentionally misled investors about its student start metrics," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation of the allege claims in the pending suit.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On September 8, 2026, investors in Stryker Corporation (NYSE: SYK) saw the price of their shares fall $26.70 (-8.8%) after the company's CFO revealed that a previously-thought resolved manufacturing issue persists. The move lower wiped out over $10 billion of Stryker's market capitalization.

The developments have prompted national shareholders rights firm Hagens Berman to open an investigation into whether Stryker was sufficiently transparent about the issue and, if not, whether the company may have violated the federal securities laws.

The firm encourages Stryker investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now. Persons with knowledge who may be able to assist the investigation are invited to contact the firm's attorneys.

Direct Contact Email: SYK@hbsslaw.com

Stryker Corporation (SYK) Investigation:

The investigation is focused on the propriety of Stryker's disclosures about its Inari Medical operations and growth prospects. Stryker acquired Inari in February 2025 to supplement Stryker's Peripheral Vascular reporting unit.

On July 30, 2026, Stryker reported its Q2 2026 results and said, without providing details, that it faced supply disruptions in the Peripheral Vascular unit and that the disruption resulted in "a meaningful backorder situation with lost sales in the quarter." Nonetheless, management assured investors that "[w]e have addressed the issue and backorder should reach a manageable level by the end of Q3."

During the related earnings call that day, an analyst asked for some color on the disruption and what exactly happened. CEO Kevin Lobo said, "I'm not going to get into the details of what it was, but let's just say it did cause a significant backorder specific to one plant in the Inari business," and "[t]he backorder is pretty elevated right now."

In response, the market sent the price of Stryker shares down $22.34 (-6.4%) the next day.

Then, during the September 8, 2026 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference, CFO Preston Wells further described the manufacturing issue as "not allowing us to reach a full supply of inventory at all of our customers[]" and "quite frankly, not allowing us to go out and really win new business."

Most concerning was his revelation that, in contrast to previous assurances, the problem "is continuing into the third quarter and will certainly continue – we expect it to continue a little bit into the fourth quarter as well."

The market negatively reacted again, sending the price of Stryker shares sharply lower that day.

"We're focused on when Stryker knew its Peripheral Vascular manufacturing problem hadn't been resolved and would persist beyond Q3," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation.

Fervo Energy Company (FRVO) Scrutinized in New Report Questioning Geothermal Narrative, Stock Closes 46% Below IPO

Fervo Energy Company (FRVO) Scrutinized in New Report Questioning Geothermal Narrative, Stock Closes 46% Below IPO

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 30, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ: FRVO) faces renewed scrutiny amid an October 6, 2026 report published by investigative research firm Morpheus Research in which Morpheus concludes "that Fervo has failed to disclose existential issues" – namely, thermal decline, excessive water loss, and seismicity-related equipment damage.

The report triggered an intraday decline in the price of Fervo shares before recovering to close at $14.33 that day (about 46% below the price of Fervo's $27 IPO last May) and follows last August's surprise revelation that the company expected a temporary shutdown of certain transmission infrastructure it relies on to deliver electricity from its Cape Station project.

Morpheus' report has prompted national shareholders rights firm Hagens Berman to expand its investigation to include the report's conclusions and, if valid, whether Fervo was sufficiently transparent to investors in its IPO documents.

The firm encourages Fervo investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now. Persons with knowledge who may be able to assist the investigation are invited to contact the firm's attorneys.

Visit: www.hbsslaw.com/frvo
Contact the Firm Now: FRVO@hbsslaw.com 
                                        844-916-0895
Video: https://youtu.be/wOyaIj5x5_E

Fervo Energy Company (FRVO) Investigation:

Fervo focuses on developing a next-generation form of geothermal energy called Enhanced Geothermal Systems, or "EGS," power facilities in the United States. The company has recently touted several Geothermal Framework Agreements ("GFAs") agreements with several well-known names, such as Google.

The investigation focuses on the propriety of Fervo's disclosures about Project Red, its proof-of-concept initiative to demonstrate commercial viability of its EGS, its Cape Station GeoCluster commercial project in Utah, and EGS having been "proven at scale."

Morpheus observed that, while Fervo claimed in its IPO documents that "Project Red has not experienced the kind of premature thermal decline that has long plagued traditional geothermal projects[,]" this apparently contrasts with an April 2026 GEOExPro report that Project Red's temperature decline was "a concerning rate of thermal decline if it continues."

Next, Morpheus concluded that Project Red exhibited an uneconomical water loss rate of ~30%, which is more than 30x higher than the sub-1% loss rate required for its commercial-scale ambitions. If correct, this severely undermines Fervo's claims that its EGS designs "minimize water usage" and "are expected to achieve recapture rates exceeding 99%, resulting in negligible cost and operational impact over the long term."

Last, noting that increased seismic activity has derailed ESG projects post-capex, Morpheus observed a heightened risk of this happening with Cape Station. The report cited data it said supported its conclusion that "Fervo's Cape Station Site Has Experienced At Least ~58 Yellow Level Seismic Events According To Its Published Seismic Catalogue, Which Rapidly Accelerated In Frequency And Intensity As Fervo Fracked Its Deepest Wells Yet In April 2026." If correct, this may bring into question the sufficiency of Fervo's IPO disclosures about seismicity risks.

"We're focused on the validity of Morpheus' conclusions and, whether Fervo was sufficiently transparent about its ability to deliver on its GFA power backlog," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation.
